title: Goclenius, Rudolph: Positiones de circulis coelestibus
shelf_note: No tradition or collection set; a Marburg disputation on the celestial circles (sphere doctrine) sits naturally with early modern science.
structure_note: 20 pages, all OCR'd, 13 translated. Signatures A 2 (p7) and B (p13) run in order; nothing stands out.

tr_errors.english: The entire celestial sphere
tr_errors.problem: orbis rendered 'sphere'; acceptable but loose

other.note: OCR image description of the woodcut initial is carried into the translation as a <meta> line ('Decorative woodcut initial letter 'T'…')

ocr_errors.problem: long s read as f (also 'interfecat' for 'intersecat' in §38); translation still right

tr_errors.english: stars subject to it
tr_errors.problem: 'omnes' (all) dropped in the opening fragment

tr_errors.english: ADDENDA TO THE CORONIS ->twice attached.<-
tr_errors.problem: 'vice' (in place of) read as 'twice'; the heading means 'additions attached in place of a coronis (closing flourish)'

tr_errors.english: the other truly from the region [called] Antarctic
tr_errors.problem: 'e regione' means 'opposite' (anti-arctic), not 'from the region'

tr_errors.source: Trinuni Deo gloria, an verò, trinuno Deo gloria
tr_errors.english: "Glory to the Trinune God" … or rather, "Glory to the Trinune God"
tr_errors.problem: the two forms being debated are rendered identically; only the notes keep the distinction

other.note: centring arrows '->twice attached.<-' kept in the translation text

book_verdict: Clean, accurate transcription of a short disputation; translation is faithful in the astronomy and slips only on two idioms ('vice', 'e regione') on the appendix page.

title: Gameren, Hannard van: Carmina Congratulatoria (Ingolstadt doctorate of Adam Myricianus)
shelf_note: No tradition or collection set; congratulatory Latin verse for a medical doctorate (1565) is ordinary early modern academic print.
structure_note: 16 pages, all OCR'd, 14 translated. Signatures A 3 (p5), B (p9), B iij (p13) run in order.

ocr_errors.problem: page self-tagged as handwritten; it is print
long s read as f (deferuit 'boiled down' for deseruit 'abandoned'); translation follows the right sense

tr_errors.source: Hic igitur primum de Bacca nomine lauri … Ritè creabatur dicebaturque Magister
tr_errors.english: Here, therefore, first, from the berry of the laurel He was duly created and called Master
tr_errors.problem: the 'Bacca lauri' = baccalaureus pun (first the bachelor's title, then Magister) is lost; reads as if he went straight to Master

tr_errors.english: he overcame the love of his affected fatherland
tr_errors.problem: 'affectae' rendered literally and obscurely

tr_errors.english: The Paeonian nobles
tr_errors.problem: 'leaders of the Paeonian (medical) art', i.e. physicians; 'nobles' obscures it

tr_errors.source: immensi rex, ac pater aetheris idem
tr_errors.english: the king of the immense, and the father of the ether
tr_errors.problem: 'immensi … aetheris' belong together (king and father of the boundless ether)

ocr_errors.problem: typographic turnover kept as written; harmless

other.note: woodcut-initial description shown as <meta> in the translation

book_verdict: Good transcription and a sound, readable verse translation; one moderate loss (the baccalaureate pun) and a wrong 'handwritten' self-tag on a printed page.

title: Hieronymi Mercurialis De arte gymnastica libri sex (Venice: Giunta, 1587)
shelf_note: Sevilla university library scan; Mercuriale's medical gymnastics is core early modern medicine.
structure_note: 360 pages, 360 OCR'd, 351 translated. Printed page numbers 69, 159, 248 at image pages 91, 181, 270 — a constant offset of 22, so the sequence is intact.

tr_errors.source: ἀγωνιστικὴ δὲ σώματος ἀρετὴ … πένταθλος. i. Agonistica autem corporis uirtus … qui. n. quodammodo crura
tr_errors.english: <note>The following is a translation of the Greek quote: "…"</note> "The excellence of the body in competition … For the one who is able to throw his legs Gymnastica. forward..."
tr_errors.problem: the full Aristotle quotation is translated only inside a <note>; the body text gives just the Latin gloss's opening, and the footer word 'Gymnastica.' is spliced into the sentence

tr_errors.source: eos satis atq. gymnasiorum columnis similes effecit
tr_errors.english: likened them to the columns of the gymnasium—sturdy but immobile
tr_errors.problem: 'sturdy but immobile' is added gloss

other.note: chapter heading rendered as '# ## Concerning Corrupt Gymnastics…' (broken markdown)

tr_errors.english: I am led to believe that **Astrandum** <note>This likely refers to a specific authority or a mis-transcription of "Adstruere"…</note> advised
tr_errors.problem: a word fragment carried over from the previous page is turned into a person who 'advised', with a speculative note

tr_errors.english: # BOOK THREE
tr_errors.problem: a running head promoted to an H1 heading mid-chapter

ocr_errors.problem: the Greek 'ἱδροῦν' (to sweat) read as Latin 'id est'; the Hippocratic advice loses 'and sweat'

tr_errors.english: <margin>2. Valerius Maximus, last chapter.</margin>
tr_errors.problem: Galen's De tuenda valetudine book 2 turned into an invented Valerius Maximus citation

tr_errors.source: <margin>Li. 2. ad Timot.</margin> (Theodorus Priscianus, book 2 to Timotheus)
tr_errors.english: <margin>Book 2 to Timothy</margin>
tr_errors.problem: reads like the Pauline epistle

book_verdict: Strong, fluent translation of a dense medical humanist text with accurate transcription; the translation embellishes the apparatus in places (an invented Valerius Maximus citation, a fragment made into a person).

title: Bredelo, Bartholomäus: De Die Oblationis Manipuli Primitialis ac Festo Pentecostes (1673)
shelf_note: No tradition set; a Lutheran disputation on Lev. 23 and the Pentecost reckoning, with rabbinic sources, is ordinary early modern Hebraist theology.
structure_note: 25 pages, all OCR'd, 16 translated. Signatures A 3 (p9) and B (p13) are in order.

tr_errors.english: the Year of Jubilee and of rest
tr_errors.problem: the sabbatical (remission) year blurred into the Jubilee

tr_errors.source: Neque contra Traditionarii pro sua sententia quicquam urgere possunt praeter illud
tr_errors.english: Nor can the Traditionalists urge anything against their own opinion beyond that
tr_errors.problem: 'contra' here means 'on the other side'; the Traditionalists can urge nothing FOR their opinion except this. The English says the opposite

tr_errors.source: intra tres dies hoc est, post tres dies agni praecepit manipulum inferri
tr_errors.english: within three days—that is, after three days—the lamb, he commanded the sheaf to be brought in
tr_errors.problem: 'after the three days of the lamb' garbled into a dangling 'the lamb'

book_verdict: Very good transcription; the translation is mostly faithful but reverses the sense of the key sentence on p13 (the Traditionalists' only argument), which would mislead a reader following the dispute.

title: Deckers, Jean: Tabula chronographica a capta per Pompeium Ierosolyma usque ad incensam … a Tito … urbem
shelf_note: No tradition set; a Jesuit chronological table of Roman and Jewish eras fits early modern chronology and scholarship.
structure_note: 24 images, each a two-page spread of tables (signatures Bb 3, Dd, Ee 2), all OCR'd and translated. The Bb–Ee signatures suggest this record is a section of a larger volume, not a standalone print. The OCR splits each paired-year cell into extra rows and mixes up several column headers.

ocr_errors.problem: right-hand table headers merged and shifted by one column, which produces invented headers ('Indictions with Daniel', '70 weeks of Augustus') and puts every column's numbers under the wrong label

ocr_errors.image: Olympiad 185 begins at 714 and 186 at 718 (the numbers are printed between the year cells)
ocr_errors.problem: Olympiad numbers for 710–717 are one too high

| Anni Diony. cum Dominica | Literis Iulij Caes. | Annis Passione |

ocr_errors.problem: two headers cut and recombined into three

tr_errors.english: indicate the 80th Dionysian year
tr_errors.problem: wrong year for the destruction of the Temple, carried from the OCR

tr_errors.source: Evangelica praedicatio restiterunt (image: Euangelicae praedicationi restiterunt)
tr_errors.english: the Evangelical preaching remained under the same Sacrament of the number
tr_errors.problem: sense reversed: the 42 years are those in which the Jews resisted the Gospel preaching

tr_errors.english: See Annotation XX of the <term>Iesu Thesium</term> <gloss>Theses of Jesus</gloss>
tr_errors.problem: 'XXI' split, and the 'I.' turned into an invented work 'Theses of Jesus'

book_verdict: The tables are mostly right number by number, but the column structure is unreliable (shifted and invented headers on p7). On p18 the key year LXX is misread as LXXX, and the sense of the 42-years passage is reversed. A chronologist would flag this on sight.
